content: 1. Concomitant use of fostamatinib may increase the concentrations of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates. Monitor for toxicities of the P-gp substrate drug, as dosage reduction may be required when administered concurrently with fostamatinib. 2. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the OATP1B1/3 transporter. Both fostemsavir and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, especially since QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 3. Gadobenate and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of gepirone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both gepirone and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Goserelin increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. This increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the FDA recommends reducing the dosage to half of the recommended dose if coadministered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Monitor closely. 9. Histrelin increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of ibrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. When coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 420 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease ifosfamide metabolism, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone, as a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by modulating both P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely, as systemic clearance may be influenced. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. At 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-gp, significantly increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin lactobionate and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Letermovir increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely, as antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for lumateperone-related adverse reactions. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of lurasidone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The manufacturer recommends decreasing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. Monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mavorizxafor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Mavorizxafor and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Mavorizxafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both mifepristone and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 49. Mipomersen and erythromycin lactobionate both have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) and use caution. 50. Mitotane decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor closely when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates for possible dosage adjustments. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mitoxantrone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters, which increases momelotinib plasma concentrations. This may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of montelukast by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of naldemedine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider initiating nifedipine at the lowest dose available if given concomitantly. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely.
